title: Volvo's big batteries: We drive its updated 2028 plug-in hybrids
gist: Volvo is giving the aging XC60 and XC90 another refresh rather than all-new replacements because the US hasn't electrified as expected, with the key upgrade a 37.9 kWh net battery that gives its PHEVs a 73-78 mile EPA electric range, plus an 11.2-inch infotainment screen with Gemini; US deliveries start Q1 next year with pricing unannounced. (The text mostly says model year 2028 but once says 2029.)

insights.claim: Volvo is refreshing the XC90 (2015) and XC60 (2017) again instead of building all-new replacements because the shift to EVs has been slower than its planners expected, especially in the US, while electrification in Europe and China makes new combustion-based platforms unlikely to get a full eight-year lifespan.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Automakers are stretching legacy platforms with bigger-battery PHEVs as a hedge, limiting capex while EV demand diverges by region.
insights.locator: COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world

insights.claim: Volvo's lack of a hands-free 'level 2+' system or point-to-point assist on the refreshed XC60/XC90 may reflect caution after its experience with the EX90, putting it behind Mercedes' point-to-point assist and Super Cruise-style hands-free systems on driver assistance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Volvo is lagging peers on ADAS features, a potential competitive weakness in premium SUVs.
insights.quote: Volvo’s experience with the EX90 may have left it a little gun-shy.
insights.locator: There are also some updated advanced driver-assistance

insights.claim: The refreshed Volvo XC60 and XC90 PHEVs get a 37.9 kWh net (41.2 kWh gross) battery, yielding EPA electric-only range estimates of 78 miles for the XC60 and 73 miles for the XC90.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Roughly doubled PHEV battery capacity raises per-vehicle battery cell demand even as automakers lean away from pure EVs.
insights.locator: There’s also a much bigger battery

insights.claim: Because the average driver covers fewer than 30 miles a day, Volvo's 73-78 mile electric range lets these PHEVs run a couple of days emissions-free between charges.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Large-battery PHEVs can deliver EV-like daily usage, strengthening the PHEV case in markets resisting full electrification.
insights.locator: Which is significant—when the average driver

insights.claim: The Volvo PHEV system combines a 247 hp 2.0 L four-cylinder gasoline engine with front and rear electric motors for 455 hp and 560 lb-ft, and the 2028 models are heavier than before, with Volvo expecting 67 mpge (XC60) and 61 mpge (XC90) in Hybrid mode.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Added battery weight trades off performance, a recurring engineering cost of bigger PHEV packs.
insights.locator: Both the midsize XC60 and three-row XC90

insights.claim: Recharging the 37.9 kWh Volvo PHEV pack takes about four hours on a Level 2 charger of at least 16 A, versus 27 hours on 120 V household power.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Bigger PHEV batteries make home Level 2 charger installation effectively necessary, supporting residential EVSE demand.
insights.locator: When it is time to plug it back in

insights.claim: Volvo has replaced Google Assistant with Google's Gemini in the refreshed XC60 and XC90 alongside a new 11.2-inch touchscreen; voice recognition improved and web lookups work well, but Gemini still failed at basic vehicle queries like current efficiency.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Gemini's rollout into Android Automotive cars expands Google's in-car AI footprint, but integration with vehicle data remains immature.
insights.quote: Most Ars readers will recoil at the news that Gemini has replaced the previous Google Assistant
insights.locator: As well as new interior materials

insights.claim: The refreshed XC60 and XC90 PHEVs are entering production now and reach the first US customers in Q1 next year, but Volvo has not announced pricing; with twice the battery capacity, a slight price increase is expected.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Pricing of doubled-battery PHEVs will indicate whether larger packs can be passed through to consumers without hurting demand.
insights.locator: With a battery big enough for daily driving
